findings.title: allec mandatory-sentence gate is substring-based, so a prefix edit still passes
findings.evidence: r198/v183/public_text_exception.py:18-19 checks SENTENCE and SENTENCE+" "+CLAUSE with count()/in. Mutation replacing "same weights as the earlier allec entry" with "the same weights as the earlier allec entry" in results.json: check_public_text_v183.py exit 0 (it should fail). The committed text is correct (results.json:4470 = entry sentence verbatim after the "Serving description:" label).
findings.requested_change: Optional hardening before the flip: also assert the exact "Serving description: "+SENTENCE+" "+CLAUSE span, or a word boundary before SENTENCE. The current candidate does not need to change.

findings.title: z3 endpoint text keeps internal operations wording ("guard release ... before deadline")
findings.evidence: results.json:304676 zils endpoint_condition ends "provider deletion and guard release were confirmed before deadline". To an outside reader, "guard release" and "deadline" mean nothing. The sentence is true and contains no forbidden token.
findings.requested_change: Optional: change it to "the rented VM deletion was confirmed by the provider", or drop the clause.

findings.title: z3 disclosure on the five >10 s decisions does not say plainly that they are scored as wrong
findings.evidence: results.json:304659 says "Five decisions exceeded 10 s and were answered; this observation does not change native completion accounting ... Time-limit treatment follows the frozen scoring view." The row page (preview/zils-ai-z3-mini-soup-preview.png) states "5 of them answered without error, counted as wrong". The text is true but opaque.
findings.requested_change: Optional: "...were answered; under the 10-second rule they count as wrong answers."

findings.title: allec 1,125 scored items vs 1,120 answered / 380 refused is truthful but implicit
findings.evidence: Scorer aggregates: v16.n_items=1125 (375 score-type items excluded under the supported-type rule, support.score=unsupported); calibration n choice 746 + noul 374 = 1,120 answered; so 5 supported-type refusals count as misses and 375 = all score items (open|score n=0). Public text (results.json:4470): "Refusals remain misses where their question type is supported; unsupported score questions follow the frozen scorer's supported-type rule." It never states 1,125. The wording is identical to the accepted v1.8.2 oenogarum row. The intake NOTES line "380 refusals remain misses in the 1,500 denominator" is wrong but was not published.
findings.requested_change: None required. A later plain-language pass could say "Intelligence and Calibration cover its 1,125 choice and true/false items."

findings.title: allec "Each choice item is read ... (four reads)" overgeneralises slightly
findings.evidence: Same wording as accepted oenogarum. The endpoint text limits four-order averaging to short requests and menus of at most 52 options. The preceding author sentence ("short requests are read in several option orders") qualifies it.
